Priya: Quick thread — pulling together 3 customer vignettes to use as scope lenses for the Optimize toolkit pilot. Please react with :eyes: if you can review and comment on risks/tradeoffs by EOD Monday.

Rafael: +1. Can you drop the vignettes here?

Priya: Vignette 1 — Conversational support bot: low-latency target (p99 < 150ms), high concurrency, needs streaming + small KV prefix cache. Customer is cost-sensitive and would accept ~2% quality delta if unit cost drops ~30%.

Rafael: That one pushes adaptive batching + small prefix caching. Quantization risk: 4-bit can bump hallucination / subtle quality regressions — we should gate with eval hooks.

Priya: Vignette 2 — Nightly embedding pipeline: throughput-first, latency not critical. Goal: ~10x cheaper cost. Aggressive quant (8-bit or 4-bit) is acceptable if downstream recall remains.

Sam: For embeddings 8-bit looks safe; 4-bit needs dataset-level checks. Strong +1 for eval-triggered alerts that can auto-fallback quantized paths.

Priya: Vignette 3 — Regulated document search: private deployment, accuracy must match baseline within 0.5% F1. Quantization allowed only if regression checks pass and audit logs are preserved.

Anya: Private deployments increase ops surface for caching (eviction, persistence). We need explicit SLOs for memory and cache eviction behavior in the spec.

Jordan: Proposal: map vignettes to three pilot lanes: (A) realtime low-latency advisor, (B) batch embeddings cost-optimization, (C) private/accuracy-constrained. Each lane gets: owner, acceptance criteria, top risks, and one de-risking experiment.

Priya: Owners proposal: Rafael -> A, Sam -> B, Jordan -> C. Please each reply with: 1) concise acceptance criteria (metrics + thresholds), 2) top 2 risks, 3) one short experiment to de-risk.

Rafael: For A (realtime): acceptance: p95 < 60ms, p99 < 150ms, regen rate < 1%, unit cost reduced >= 20% vs current baseline. Risks: (1) KV cache correctness/consistency under concurrent writes, (2) quantization-induced hallucination. Experiment: staging A/B test that toggles small prefix cache + adaptive batch size; measure p95/p99 and a short eval set for hallucination.

Sam: For B (embeddings): acceptance: end-to-end throughput target met with >=10x cost reduction, recall delta <= 1% on benchmark, automatic fallback when eval fails. Risks: (1) quantized representation drift for tail queries, (2) metric mismatch between bench and customer corpus. Experiment: run 100k offline embeddings across 8-bit and 4-bit variants and run recall/nearest-neighbor evals. Add an eval-triggered alert that disables quant if recall drops >0.5% over two runs.

Jordan: For C (private/reg): acceptance: F1 within 0.5% of baseline on the customer's eval set, successful KMS/HSM integration, deployment automation health checks pass. Risks: (1) KMS/HSM integration failures lengthen rollout, (2) per-tenant eval variance. Experiment: per-customer canary that applies quantization + runs the customer's eval; if drop >0.3% for 3 consecutive runs -> rollback and alert.

Priya: Nice. I'll synthesize this into a short scope doc and open pilot tickets. One immediate ask: Rafael + Sam, please draft a minimal eval-triggered alert proto in this thread — something actionable and simple, e.g. "if primary eval metric drops >0.3% for 3 consecutive runs -> auto-disable quant and page oncall". Include cadence and dataset for that alert.

Rafael: Agree. I'll draft alert def but need to confirm eval cadence (daily vs on-deploy). My suggestion: run nightly evals for batch lane, and per-deploy + nightly for realtime lane.

Sam: I'll attach recommended benchmark sets tomorrow (small, medium, and long-tail). +1 on auto-disable; also propose a soft-warning on first failure (email/console) before auto-disable to collect telemetry.

optimize-bot: New ticket created: OPT-7241 "Pilot lanes: vignettes -> acceptance criteria" assigned to Priya. :robot_face:

Priya: Thanks all. If no objections, I'll lock scope by Wed and prepare kickoff doc + acceptance checklist.

Rafael: No objections from me.

Sam: Sounds good.

Anya: 👍

Jordan: On it — will draft automation checklist for private lane.
